
Two arXiv papers from the RSS feed meet ≥3 inclusion criteria with meaningful harness-layer contributions: SeerGuard (safety constraint infrastructure for GUI agents via world-model prediction) and ToolVerse (massive execution environment harness for agentic RL with long-horizon tool tasks). Grok social signals were either already in the README or unverifiable. All other arXiv papers were application-logic or capability-focused without substantive harness-layer contributions.

## Suggestions

- [SeerGuard: A Safety Framework for Mobile GUI Agents via World Model Prediction](https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.15550) — Harness-layer safety framework for mobile GUI agents that uses world model prediction to anticipate and gate unsafe actions before execution, providing proactive constraint enforcement at the scaffolding level.
  Section: Research Papers > Safety & Constraint Infrastructure | Criteria: Manages safety constraints at the harness layer (world-model-based action gating before execution), Evaluates agent behavior through controlled harness-mediated interactions (GUI agent safety evaluation), Empirical evidence of harness safety design improving agent safety outcomes

- [ToolVerse: Unlocking Massive Environments and Long-Horizon Tasks for Agentic Reinforcement Learning](https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.15660) — Defines a large-scale execution environment and tool harness for agentic RL, providing controlled multi-tool dispatch infrastructure and long-horizon task scaffolding with empirical evaluation of agent performance.
  Section: Research Papers > Tool & API Integration Layers | Criteria: Defines execution environments and scaffolding that host AI agents across massive tool spaces, Manages tool dispatch and state management at the harness layer for long-horizon tasks, Evaluates agent behavior through controlled harness-mediated interactions with empirical results
